title: Maximin Power for Detecting Any Superior Dose in Three-Arm Binary Trials
banked_reason: D0.5 validity gate confirmed a mathematically sound incremental finite-frontier package, but the all-size structural evaluator remains open and cannot meet the fixed field floor through a bounded repair.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution consists of an exact orbit-capacity optimization representation, certificate and contact machinery, selected matched finite values, a small endpoint branch and a sufficient perfect-power regime; it does not evaluate the general all-design frontier. The TL;DR describes an evaluated all-size map and its outputs as the constructive headline, but structural-frontier leaves that map, its transitions and its termination open, so this is a stale overclaim. The perfect-power equivalence still requires optimizing an assignment law, and the Hoeffding stopping bound supplies conservative achievability rather than the missing exact frontier. The evaluated planning examples concern tiny rosters, maximal improvement or ten-percent power, leaving the advertised prospective planning significance undemonstrated and constraining the paper score to 4.3. The scope paragraph also rejects the newer n=5,k≤3 and n=6,k≤4 values despite their supplied certificates; an independent exhaustive rational replay confirms the displayed n=5,k=2 certificate, so this inconsistency requires correction rather than blanket rejection of those results. Published [Singh–Davidov](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378375826000078) theorem comparisons remain a source-verification item because only publisher summaries and snippets were accessible; unpublished repository donors lack independently inspected archival theorem text, and neither access limitation alone determines this below-field assessment. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 4.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

Construct a deletion-closed saddle family that retains nonsharp null components, inactive-dose response variation and capacity-binding contacts, using the supplied n=5 and n=6 certificates to test closure. Prove that its explicit transitions preserve every verifier inequality and produce matching certificates for all n,k, with termination and bit-complexity bounds.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived exact orbit-capacity and saddle/contact machinery, a finite matched frontier through n=5 with selected n=6 cases, endpoint/perfect-power branches, and finite planning termination. The validity gate exhaustively replayed the four disputed certificates and resolved the contradiction as stale prose, then corrected the scope and regenerated the writeup. The all-size deletion-closed evaluator, transition laws, termination/bit-complexity guarantees, general iid attainment and realistic planning benchmark remain unresolved; the sound incremental package cannot meet the fixed field floor. No F-stage Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: Two active doses share one control roster, and the scientific decision is whether either dose improves a binary response. The focal object \(B_n(k)\) is the guaranteed power attainable by any ex ante assignment law and any total original-record test at maximal weak-null size \(1/20\), for the integer improvement count \(k\) fixed in the protocol. We prove an exact representation of this full labelled testing game by its orbit-capacity primal, a compatible-mixture saddle verifier and complete contact identities. Exact rational certificates evaluate the complete frontier through five units and selected six-unit cases, while analytic endpoint, perfect-power and finite-planning results describe further branches. An evaluated all-size structural map and a general classification of attaining independent allocations remain open.
gap: Exact maximin tests, optimized multiple testing, finite-population weak-null inference and response-type games already exist. The inspected results do not evaluate the simultaneous compatible-table and assignment-capacity saddle for detecting an unknown superior dose over all assignment laws.
fill: The constructive contribution is the evaluated structural map \(\mathcal E(n,k)\) and its rational certificate \((w,\nu,\lambda,\mu,b)\), including the mixture and contact transitions. The exact original-record representation and generic finite program supply supporting verification. The evaluated outputs certify \(B_n(k)\), implement an exactly calibrated procedure, characterize attaining allocations and evaluate \(N\) and \(K\).
